name: Persistent storage (persist)
plain: Asks the browser not to delete this site's stored data under disk pressure.
meaning: Protects offline data (notes, drafts, downloaded media) from automatic eviction. Chrome and Safari decide silently from engagement; Firefox asks the person. A grant does not raise the quota.

access.prompt_ui: Firefox: bubble Store data in persistent storage, Allow or Don't allow. Chrome and Safari: no prompt, granted by heuristics (installed, bookmarked, notifications on, high engagement).
access.persistence: Persistent until cleared by the person
steps: Data is exempt from best-effort eviction

limits.headline: Can ask the browser not to delete its saved data when disk space is low
limits.user_action: In Firefox you click Allow on Store data in persistent storage. Elsewhere nothing: the browser decides.
can: Ask the browser to protect its saved data from automatic cleanup
Check whether the request was granted
Check roughly how much space it has used
cannot: Make the browser agree, since Chrome and Safari decide on their own
Stop you clearing site data yourself
Keep data after a private window closes
limits.differs: Firefox asks you. Chrome and Safari give it quietly, based on signs like installing the site, a bookmark or heavy use.

story.what_it_is: Asks the browser not to delete this site's stored data when your disk runs low.

marketing.name: Persistent storage
marketing.pitch: Google explains how a web app can ask to keep its data safe from cleanup.

marketing.name: StorageManager persist
marketing.pitch: Documents the call a site makes to ask for protected storage.

story.for_you: In some browsers a small prompt asks 'Allow this site to store data in your browser?' In Chrome the decision is automatic, based on use and bookmarks. You usually just see nothing.
story.for_makers: It protects work that is only on the device, like drafts, saves and offline files. Makers ask when losing data would hurt trust. The browser may decline.

use_cases.example: A browser game asks to protect your save file so you do not lose hours of play.
A note taking app asks to keep your offline notes before they sync.
A web design or music tool asks to keep a long local project.
A web music or reading app asks to keep your downloaded content.
A field work app asks to protect forms filled out without a signal.
A health diary web app asks to keep entries safe on your device.

technical_bounds: Chrome and Safari give no prompt: the answer is automatic
Safari still clears script-written data after 7 days without interaction unless installed
